critical_code_review_comments: routes/auth.py:login/register — set_auth_cookie is called BEFORE the response is returned: good. But the token is ALSO returned in the JSON body. With the move to HttpOnly cookies, returning the JWT in the body is now redundant and slightly weakens the XSS-protection benefit (a stolen XSS payload can still read the token from the response if it intercepts fetch). Consider returning only {user:…} once frontend stops reading `data.token`.

server.py:get_current_user lines 167-179: when a JWT happens to collide with an existing session_token (extremely unlikely but possible), the session_token branch is tried first and might wrongly return a stale user. Low risk because session_token is server-generated random by Emergent, but worth a comment.
server.py:149-151 clear_auth_cookie uses samesite='none', secure=True — matches set_auth_cookie. Good.

rca of the issue: CORS Allow-Origin '*' with Allow-Credentials 'true': raw curl OPTIONS to /api/auth/login returns BOTH headers simultaneously, which Starlette's CORSMiddleware will never produce (it's coded to echo the specific Origin or omit the header entirely when credentials are allowed). Therefore the contradictory pair must be injected by an upstream proxy (Cloudflare/k8s ingress on emergentagent.com). Reproduction: `curl -i -X OPTIONS https://joblink-stages.preview.emergentagent.com/api/auth/login -H 'Origin: https://joblink-stages.preview.emergentagent.com' -H 'Access-Control-Request-Method: POST'` → see both headers. Mitigation: (1) remove the ingress-level CORS rewrite, OR (2) configure the ingress to echo the request Origin when credentials are present. App works today only because frontend and backend share the exact same origin and the browser does NOT enforce CORS on same-origin requests.
